_comment: Routine names supported by evidence, applied by tools/disasm_all.py. Key 'BB:AAAA'. A name describes what the routine provably does (read from its instructions, or confirmed on the emulator) and never a guessed game purpose. 'note' gives inputs and outputs. The address name (Func_BBB_AAAA) is kept as an alias label. Evidence ids refer to docs/EVIDENCE_LOG.md; 'reading' means a complete static reading of the routine's instructions (E-0022).

00:000E.name: JumpToHL
00:000E.note: jp hl; the call target used by CallInBank

00:0080.name: InstallOamDmaRoutine
00:0080.note: copies the 10 bytes at $008E (ld a,$C0 / ldh [rDMA],a / wait / ret) to HRAM at $FF80

00:0949.name: FillBytes
00:0949.note: A = value, HL = destination, BC = count; HL ends past the last byte (memset)

00:0952.name: CopyBytes
00:0952.note: HL = source, DE = destination, BC = count (memcpy)

00:095B.name: NextTableByte
00:095B.note: wC5E8 = (wC5E8 + 1) & $7F; wC5E7 = the byte at $0973 + wC5E8

00:05D1.name: SpinDelay
00:05D1.note: returns at once if wC524 is zero, otherwise counts DE from $1B58 to 0 with three nops per step

00:120A.name: WaitForVRAMAccess
00:120A.note: loops until STAT bit 1 is clear (modes 0 and 1); returns with Z set

00:1211.name: WriteVRAMByte
00:1211.note: A = value, HL = address; disables interrupts, waits until VRAM is accessible, stores A at [HL]; clobbers hFFD1

00:121F.name: WriteVRAMByteInc
00:121F.note: like WriteVRAMByte but stores at [HL] and increments HL

00:1278.name: QueueSoundEffect
00:1278.note: wSoundEffectRequest = A; ProcessSoundQueue starts it on the next frame

00:1682.name: Multiply8
00:1682.note: HL = A * C (8 x 8 bit); clobbers A, B and C

00:16D1.name: DivideHLByA
00:16D1.note: HL = HL / A (quotient in HL), A = remainder; clobbers D, E

00:16F5.name: HLToDecimalDigits
00:16F5.note: HL (0-999) becomes three digits: wC8C0 = hundreds, wC8C1 = tens, wC8C2 = ones

00:181B.name: TestFlagBit
00:181B.note: DE = bit number; tests that bit of the bit array at wCBD7 (bit 0 of the first byte first); returns carry set when it is 1, A = 0 and carry clear otherwise; no range check

00:1845.name: SetFlagBit
00:1845.note: DE = bit number; sets that bit of the bit array at wCBD7; does nothing when DE >= $0300

00:1872.name: ReadByteInBank
00:1872.note: B = ROM bank, DE = address; C = the byte at [DE] in that bank; the caller's bank is restored

00:1F80.name: LoadSRAMRecordByte
00:1F80.note: A = record, C = offset; hFFC6 = the byte at sA000 + A * $A5 + C; HL preserved

00:1F89.name: LoadSRAMRecordWord
00:1F89.note: like LoadSRAMRecordByte but loads the word into hFFC6 (low) and hFFC7 (high)

00:1FD1.name: SRAMRecordAddress
00:1FD1.note: A = record, C = offset; HL = sA000 + A * $A5 + C (records are $A5 bytes)

00:290E.name: FillTilesFromRequest
00:290E.note: fills a block of tiles at wC52D/wC52E with the 16-byte pattern at $2940: width wC52F, height wC530 tiles (each byte waits for VRAM access); returns at once if either is zero

00:2E98.name: FillTilesRequest
00:2E98.note: HL = destination, DE = size (E = width, D = height); stores them and calls FillTilesFromRequest

00:3E7A.name: CompareHLToBC
00:3E7A.note: Z set when HL == BC; A is clobbered

00:3F25.name: AddAx9ToHL
00:3F25.note: HL += (A * 9) & $FF (the product is computed in 8 bits and wraps); A is clobbered, other registers preserved

13:4001.name: StartMessageCommand09HL_B13
13:4001.note: starts a message through script command $09 (message word HL, shown by the same group dispatch as ShowMessageHL when wD7F0 = 0): HL is stored in wScriptParam0 (low) and wScriptParam1 (high); then wC5DC = 1, wC920 = 9, wC91F = 1, wC923 = 0 and wC919 = 0 (an earlier store of $80 to wC919 is overwritten)

04:55BB.name: StartMessageCommand09HL_B04
04:55BB.note: starts a message through script command $09 (message word HL, shown by the same group dispatch as ShowMessageHL when wD7F0 = 0): HL is stored in wScriptParam0 (low) and wScriptParam1 (high); then wC5DC = 1, wC920 = 9, wC91F = 1, wC923 = 0 and wC919 = 0 (an earlier store of $80 to wC919 is overwritten)

13:4049.name: StartScriptAtHL_B13
13:4049.note: HL is stored in wScriptPointerLo/Hi; then wScriptStartRequest = $80 and wModeState = 1, so the script engine starts fetching at HL (E-0082)

04:5603.name: StartScriptAtHL_B04
04:5603.note: HL is stored in wScriptPointerLo/Hi; then wScriptStartRequest = $80 and wModeState = 1, so the script engine starts fetching at HL (E-0082)

0F:7F68.name: StartMessageHL_B0F
0F:7F68.note: HL is stored in wC924 (low) and wC925 (high); then wC926 = 0

73:4ED8.name: StartMessageHL_B73
73:4ED8.note: HL is stored in wC924 (low) and wC925 (high); then wC926 = 0

04:55DF.name: StartMessageScriptDE_B04
04:55DF.note: starts a message through script command $0A: DE is stored in wMessageIndex (low) and wMessageGroup (high); then wC5DC = 1, wC920 = $0A, wC91F = 1, wC923 = 0 and wC919 = 0 (an earlier store of $80 is overwritten)

13:4025.name: StartMessageScriptDE_B13
13:4025.note: starts a message through script command $0A: DE is stored in wMessageIndex (low) and wMessageGroup (high); then wC5DC = 1, wC920 = $0A, wC91F = 1, wC923 = 0 and wC919 = 0 (an earlier store of $80 is overwritten)

0F:7ECE.name: SetBit2AtHL_B0F
0F:7ECE.note: sets bit 2 of the byte at [HL]; only A is clobbered

73:7A47.name: SetBit2AtHL_B73
73:7A47.note: sets bit 2 of the byte at [HL]; only A is clobbered

12:65F5.name: SetBit2AtHL_B12
12:65F5.note: sets bit 2 of the byte at [HL]; only A is clobbered

00:3E54.name: CarryUnlessWDA63SlotEmpty
00:3E54.note: A = slot number; returns with carry clear only when A < 8 and wDA63[A] is zero (carry set for A >= 8, for $FF and for any other non-zero value); A, BC and HL are preserved

08:4032.name: StringDatabase
08:4032.note: nine pointers, one per string category; each points at a table of string pointers; strings end in $F0 (E-0026)

08:4044.name: StringTable_System

00:08BA.note: A is stored in rSB and rSC becomes $80 (transfer start, external clock); interrupts are off during the write

00:2E40.name: LookupString
00:2E40.note: DE = table of 16-bit pointers, one per category; wC528 = category, wC529 = index; returns DE = the string pointer; stores the current ROM bank in wC52A

00:25C9.name: BeginStringDisplay
00:25C9.note: DE = string table (see LookupString); clears the request area with FillTilesFromRequest, copies the position wC52D/wC52E to wC531/wC532 and wC535/wC536, points wC533/wC534 and wC537/wC538 at the string, sets wC52B = 1 and clears wC52C and wC54F; the string is drawn later by the routine at $2620

00:25FE.name: CopyStringToBuffer

00:2611.name: RunStringDisplayToEnd
00:2611.note: sets bit 1 of wC52B, then runs the display step at $2620 until wC52B is zero

00:16AA.name: Multiply8By16
00:16AA.note: E:H:L = A * BC (24-bit product); clobbers A, BC, HL, E

00:16BF.name: DivideBByA
00:16BF.note: B = B / A (quotient), A = remainder; clobbers D, E

00:16E2.name: Divide24ByA
00:16E2.note: E:H:L = E:H:L / A (24-bit quotient), A = remainder; clobbers B, D

F0:7C51.name: AddBClampedToC
F0:7C51.note: [HL] = min([HL] + B, C) (8-bit add, no overflow check); clobbers A, C

F0:7C5B.name: SubtractBClampedAtZero
F0:7C5B.note: [HL] = [HL] - B, or 0 when the result has bit 7 set; clobbers A

00:1F49.name: SRAMRecordAddressMapped
00:1F49.note: A is first passed through MapIndexViaWC6FE; then HL = sA000 + A * $A5 + C as in SRAMRecordAddress

00:24C5.name: MapIndexViaWC6FE
00:24C5.note: returns A unchanged when wC58A is non-zero and wC5DB is 4; otherwise A = the byte at wC6FE + (A & $7F); HL is clobbered in that case

00:1881.name: FillTilesBxC
00:1881.note: HL = destination, B = width, C = height: writes the 16-byte pattern at $2940 B * C times, each byte after waiting for VRAM access; wC52D holds B between rows

E2:651C.name: AddBCToWordAtHL
E2:651C.note: the 16-bit word at [HL] += BC; HL is unchanged

E2:654B.name: ReadBank6TableWord
E2:654B.note: BC = the 16-bit word at ROM bank 6, $4001 + $36 * BC + 2 * wD2C7 (rows of 27 words); A = its low byte; clobbers HL, E

E2:64CE.name: AccumulateBank6WordToDA6E
E2:64CE.note: word = ReadBank6TableWord; if its low byte is $FF the value is 5000, which is added to wDA6E; a positive word is added to wDA6E; a negative word's magnitude is added to wDA70

E2:64F5.name: AccumulateBank6WordToDA70
E2:64F5.note: the mirror of AccumulateBank6WordToDA6E: $FF (5000) and positive words go to wDA70, negative words' magnitude goes to wDA6E

E0:7420.name: DrawSpriteSlots
E0:7420.note: for each of the wSpriteSlotCount 8-byte slots at wSpriteSlots: loads hSpriteSetIndex, hSpriteOriginX (+8), hSpriteOriginY, hSpriteAttrXor, hSpriteTileOffset and hSpriteSubIndex from the slot, then far-calls the routine chosen by the slot's first byte from the 3-byte entries at $7477

E0:7480.name: IncrementSpriteSlotCounters
E0:7480.note: adds 1 to byte 7 of each of the 8 slots at wSpriteSlots

E0:7492.name: StepSpriteSlotToward
E0:7492.note: A = slot number, D = target X, E = target Y: moves the slot's X and Y bytes one step toward the target and adds 1 to its byte 7; returns A = 1 (non-zero) if either moved

E0:74C5.name: SetSpriteSlotByte5
E0:74C5.note: A = slot number: byte 5 of the slot = C

E0:754F.name: StepWD0A2Mod15
E0:754F.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 15

E0:755E.name: StepWD0A2Mod30
E0:755E.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 30

E0:756D.name: StepWD0A2Mod45
E0:756D.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 45

E0:757C.name: StepWD0A2Mod60
E0:757C.note: wD0A2 += 1, reset to 0 when it reaches 60

00:0DF2.name: StartPaletteFade
00:0DF2.note: A = level (bit 7 set selects the second form); on CGB it hands over to Func_002_4001; on DMG it rebuilds the palette copy at wC4FF from wC4DF and sets wC56C, wC572-wC574, with $7FFF (white) or $0000 (black) fill chosen by bit 7 of wC56D; observed writes only, the purpose is a palette fade by inference

03:42DA.name: CopyTileBufferToBGMap
03:42DA.note: copies the 20 x 18 tiles at the start of wScreenTileBuffer to vBGMap0 (CopyRectToBGMap with BC = $1412)

03:42E3.name: CopyRectToBGMap
03:42E3.note: HL = BG map address, DE = source, B = width, C = rows: writes B bytes per row with WriteVRAMByte (HL wraps inside its 32-entry row, then the source and destination each move down 32 and HL is masked with $9B)

00:21A1.name: CopyGlyphTilesToVRAM
00:21A1.note: DE = VRAM destination: for each byte of the string at wC8CF (up to 11, stopping at $F0), copies the 16-byte tile at ROM bank $1F, $4010 + 16 * character to [DE]; the characters $8D and $8E also OR a 16-byte overlay from $48E0 or $48F0 into the previous tile

33:4001.name: CopyBlockToTileBuffer
33:4001.note: DE = block number: the table at $405F gives each block an offset into wScreenTileBuffer (word), a width B and a height C, followed by B * C tile bytes; they are copied into wScreenTileBuffer rows 32 bytes apart

5F:6BCD.name: AddStepDeltaToPointedByte
5F:6BCD.note: the byte at the address in wC928/wC929 += the byte at Func_05F_6BE8 + wC921 / 2

00:2123.name: WriteDecimalDigitTiles
00:2123.note: DE = destination: writes three tile ids for the digits in wC8C0-wC8C2 (see HLToDecimalDigits): $E0 + digit, with leading zeros as $C3; DE ends past the third

12:7DCE.name: FindHFFC6InWC61DList
12:7DCE.note: hFFC6 = the index of the first byte of the 24-entry list at wC61D equal to hFFC6; $FF when an entry is $00 or $FF first or no entry matches

00:173A.name: Number24ToPackedBCD
00:173A.note: the 24-bit value at wC8C0-wC8C2 (low byte first) becomes decimal digits: hFFC9 = millions, hFFC8 = hundred-thousands and ten-thousands, hFFC7 = thousands and hundreds, hFFC6 = tens and ones (two digits per byte, high digit in the upper nibble); wC8C0-wC8C2 are consumed

00:1FA4.name: CopyRecordNameToWC8CF
00:1FA4.note: A = record number, C = offset (see SRAMRecordAddress): copies 10 bytes from the SRAM record to wC8CF; when the first byte is $FF it writes $98,$98,$98,$90,$90 instead and sets carry; DE and HL are preserved

F1:5834.name: BeginString_Bank0E_Cat0
F1:5834.note: A = string index: wStringIndex = A, wStringCategory = 0, then BeginStringDisplay_Bank0E

1F:5040.name: SendSGBPacketSet
1F:5040.note: returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise sends the packet set chosen by wSGBPacketIndex ($FF = the buffer at wSGBPacketBuffer, else the pointer in the table at $5094): the packet count is the first byte's low 3 bits, each 16-byte packet is sent through rP1 as a $00/$30 reset pulse, 128 bits (a 1 bit is written as $10, a 0 bit as $20, each followed by $30) and a stop bit
1F:5040.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:05E2.name: DetectSGB
00:05E2.note: sends packet set $0B, reads rP1 with two different line selections and returns carry set when the joypad lines change as a Super Game Boy makes them; sends packet set $0A afterwards in both outcomes
00:05E2.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0692.name: DelayBCWhenSGB
00:0692.note: returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise busy-waits BC times about $06D6 loop passes

00:0796.name: TurnOffLCD
00:0796.note: if rLCDC bit 7 is set, waits for rLY = $91, then clears rLCDC bit 7 and bit 7 of wC5EC

00:06A8.name: SGBTransferCompressed
00:06A8.note: A = packet set index (stored in wSGBPacketIndex); returns at once when wSGBActive is 0; otherwise turns the LCD off, clears vTiles1, decompresses the stream at HL into vTiles1, fills the 20 x 13 corner of vBGMap0 with tiles $80, $81, ... in order, turns the LCD on, sends the packet set with SendSGBPacketSet and turns it off again; the tile data is thereby shown for the Super Game Boy to read
00:06A8.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0705.name: SGBTransferRaw
00:0705.note: A = packet set index; H = ROM bank, DE = source, BC = byte count: the same as SGBTransferCompressed, but copies the bytes to vTiles1 instead of decompressing
00:0705.evidence: reading; Super Game Boy packet protocol (Pan Docs) for the bit pattern

00:0829.name: UploadBGPalettes
00:0829.note: when bit 7 of wC526 is set, writes 8 bytes (one palette) from a buffer address derived by Func_000_0897 to rBGPD starting at index wC526; otherwise writes all 64 bytes from wC49F to rBGPD from index 0; each byte is written after waiting for VRAM access

00:3290.name: InitSoundHardware
00:3290.note: rNR52 = $80, rNR51 = 0, rNR50 = $77; sets the first two bytes of each of the 6 channel slots at wSoundChannelSlots to $FF; clears the 72 bytes at wSoundLabelSlots, wDD15 and wDD19; calls Func_000_32DB with BC = 0

00:0040.name: VBlankVector
00:0040.note: di; jp VBlankHandler (the interrupt vector at $0040)

00:03A4.name: VBlankHandler
00:03A4.note: runs once per frame: saves registers and the VRAM and WRAM banks; skips everything but the sound tick when wC5ED bit 0 shows it was entered again; otherwise runs the OAM DMA routine at $FF80, uploads queued palettes on CGB, flushes the queued BG map write, restores the DMG palettes, scroll and LCDC, applies the screen shake, polls the joypad, runs SoundTick, advances the random seed, processes the sound queue, runs GameFrameUpdate, steps the string display when wC52B is set, steps the fade, and increments the 16-bit frame counter wC5F0/wC5F1; resets the game when all four buttons are held

00:33E8.name: SoundTick
00:33E8.note: for each of the 6 channel slots at wSoundChannelSlots: copies the slot into HRAM $FFD8-$FFF7, reads events from the track in bank hSoundBank and writes the channel's sound registers (the per-frame sound engine; called from VBlankHandler)

00:131A.name: ProcessSoundQueue
00:131A.note: starts the music requested in wMusicRequest and the effect requested in wSoundEffectRequest (StartMusic / StartSoundEffect), then sets each request to $FF

00:1231.name: StartMusic
00:1231.note: A = sound id (0 = none): stores it in wC608, calls InitSoundHardware (silencing every channel), stores A in wSoundId and starts the track with Func_000_334E unless the id is one of a list that is handled separately

00:127C.name: StartSoundEffect
00:127C.note: A = sound id: stores it in wSoundId and starts the effect (ids in a fixed list take a separate path)

00:0474.name: GameFrameUpdate
00:0474.note: hOamNextEntry = 0, ComputeSpriteScrollOffsets, RunGameModeUpdate, and ClearUnusedOAMEntries unless a fade is running

00:048A.name: RunGameModeUpdate
00:048A.note: unless wC5DF is non-zero or a fade is running: jumps through a 9-entry table indexed by wGameMode to the mode's per-frame routine (modes 0-8 in banks $01, $02, $03, none, $31, $07, $24, $A0, $F2)

00:0355.name: RunGameModeInit
00:0355.note: jumps through a 9-entry table indexed by wGameMode to the mode's start-up routine (banks $01, $02, $03, none, $31, $07, $24, $A0, $F2); called from the main loop each time the mode changes

00:0BB4.name: ClearUnusedOAMEntries
00:0BB4.note: zeroes the first byte (Y) of every OAM shadow entry from hOamNextEntry up to 40

00:252D.name: ComputeSpriteScrollOffsets
00:252D.note: hFFD2/hFFD3 = -(hScrollX - 9) - 1 and hFFD4/hFFD5 = -(hScrollY - $11) - 1 as 16-bit values; returns early in game mode 1 when wC5DC & $0F = 6

00:0BCC.name: FlushQueuedBGMapWrite
00:0BCC.note: if wC0C0/wC0C1 (a VRAM address) is non-zero, writes wC0C3 bytes from wC0C4 there: along the row when wC0C2 is 0, down the column otherwise

00:04ED.name: ApplyScreenShake
00:04ED.note: while wC604 or wC605 is non-zero, counts it down and adds an oscillating offset (from the counter's low bits) to rSCY or rSCX

00:07FD.name: CopyDMGPalettesToHardware
00:07FD.note: rBGP, rOBP0, rOBP1 = wC5E9, wC5EA, wC5EB

00:07F1.name: WriteLCDCShadow
00:07F1.note: waits until rSTAT mode bits are 0, then rLCDC = wC5EC

00:0F4E.name: StepFade
00:0F4E.note: does nothing when wFadeState is 0; otherwise advances the palette fade by one step per call (CGB, SGB and DMG paths)

00:0A61.name: ReadJoypadDirect
00:0A61.note: B = the buttons: upper nibble D-pad (bit 7 down, 6 up, 5 left, 4 right), lower nibble A, B, Select, Start (bits 0-3), 1 = pressed; reads rP1 with each line group selected

00:0A17.name: PollJoypad
00:0A17.note: shifts wJoypadHeld to wJoypadHeldPrev and reads the new state into wJoypadHeld (directly, or through the SGB path when wSGBActive)

00:0A8D.name: UpdateJoypadPresses
00:0A8D.note: wJoypadPressed = buttons newly held since the last poll; wJoypadPressedRepeat = the same, plus an auto-repeat that fires after $14 frames and then every 6 (timer in wJoypadRepeatTimer)

01:4001.name: GameMode0_Init
01:4001.note: start-up for wGameMode = 0; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: debug menu (E-0029)

02:45C6.name: GameMode1_Init
02:45C6.note: start-up for wGameMode = 1; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: water map with the player sprite (E-0029)

03:4001.name: GameMode2_Init
03:4001.note: start-up for wGameMode = 2; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: monster status panel (incomplete when forced) (E-0029)

31:4001.name: GameMode4_Init
31:4001.note: start-up for wGameMode = 4, the battle: starts music 2, clears the BG map and builds the battle screen; reached from the debug battle setup (Start) and from encounters (E-0042)

31:40A5.name: GameMode4_Update
31:40A5.note: per-frame routine for wGameMode = 4, the battle: in link mode (wC58A) it serves the serial link, otherwise IncrementPlayTime_Bank31 and the phase machine Func_031_40CC (wCFC8 = phase (1 fight, 2 after), wCFC9 = step)

07:486E.name: GameMode5_Init
07:486E.note: start-up for wGameMode = 5; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: title screen; also sparkles and a victory screen when forced (E-0029)

24:4001.name: GameMode6_Init
24:4001.note: start-up for wGameMode = 6; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: victory screen when forced (E-0029)

A0:4ECF.name: GameMode7_Init
A0:4ECF.note: start-up for wGameMode = 7; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: two monster panels when forced (E-0029)

F2:4001.name: GameMode8_Init
F2:4001.note: start-up for wGameMode = 8; forcing this mode on the emulator shows: egg-received dialogue when forced (E-0029)

02:5F59.name: IncrementPlayTime
02:5F59.note: counts frames wC82D (0-59), seconds wC82E (0-59), minutes wC82F (0-59) and a 16-bit hour count wC830/wC831; stops at 999:59:59 ($03E7 hours)

02:541B.name: UpdatePlayerMovement
02:541B.note: does nothing during a fade or while the map is loading; reads the D-pad (wJoypadHeld, wJoypadPressed), sets the facing hPlayerFacing and the move timer hFF9A, and starts or continues a step when the tile ahead is free (checks through Func_002_59CD, Func_002_5A51 and Func_002_5AB6)

02:4FE8.name: CheckInteractionInFront
02:4FE8.note: when A is newly pressed and no fade, load or move is in progress: finds the position one step ahead of the player (hPlayerX or hPlayerY +/- 16 chosen by hPlayerFacing), looks it up with Func_002_59CD, and compares the result with the four ids at wC910 to pick an interaction

12:6EC6.name: DrawFieldSprites
12:6EC6.note: unless the map is loading or wCBCF bit 7 is clear: reads the sprite entries starting at wCBCF (tile offset, set index with bit 7 selecting a sub index, attribute, position bytes), sets the hSprite inputs and 16-bit positions from them plus the scroll, and draws each with DrawMetaSprite

7F:700A.name: DrawMetaSprite
7F:700A.note: DE = Data_07F_7011 (the table of meta-sprite sets), then DrawMetaSpriteAt

7F:7065.name: DrawMetaSpriteAt
7F:7065.note: DE = table of set pointers: returns at once when hOamNextEntry is $27 or more; otherwise converts the 16-bit position (hSpriteOriginX with hFFAA, hSpriteOriginY with hFFAC) to screen coordinates by adding the scroll-offset words hSpriteScrollXLo/Hi and hSpriteScrollYLo/Hi, and writes OAM entries for the sprite chosen by hSpriteSetIndex and hSpriteSubIndex (tile += hSpriteTileOffset, attribute ^= hSpriteAttrXor)

02:59CD.name: TileBlockedAtPixel
02:59CD.note: B = X, C = Y in pixels: copies the four tile ids of the 2 x 2 block at tile (X / 8, Y / 8) of wScreenTileBuffer (rows of 20) to wC910-wC913; returns A = 1 when any of them is at most wC192, else A = 0 (a different pair of comparisons with wC196 runs when hFF8C bit 3 is set)

02:5A51.name: FindSpriteSlotAtTile
02:5A51.note: B = X, C = Y in pixels: returns A = the 1-based number of the first slot of wSpriteSlots (from wCB8A, count wSpriteSlotCount) whose X and Y bytes, or those plus 15, lie in the same 16-pixel cell as (B, C); A = 0 when none does

33:5550.name: BeginString_Bank07_Cat5
33:5550.note: A = string index: wStringIndex = A, wStringCategory = 5, then BeginStringDisplay_Bank07

F0:5DDD.name: BeginString_BankF0_Cat0
F0:5DDD.note: A = string index: wStringIndex = A, wStringCategory = 0, then BeginStringDisplay_BankF0_48A0

1B:61F5.name: BeginString_Bank1B_Cat0
1B:61F5.note: A = string index: wStringIndex = A, wStringCategory = 0, then BeginStringDisplay_Bank1B_480C

00:23BD.name: GradeHFFC6
00:23BD.note: C = 0 when hFFC6 >= $C0, 1 when hFFC6 >= $40, otherwise 2

00:2391.name: PersonalityIndexOfRecord
00:2391.note: A = SRAM record number: grades the record's bytes at offsets $6F, $72 and $70 with GradeHFFC6 (g1, g2, g3, each 0-2) and returns A = 9 * g1 + 3 * g2 + g3, a number from 0 to 26. The status screen passes this to the string database as a personality-name index (category 7, 27 names), so it is the monster's personality index (E-0031)

1A:4001.name: LoadSkillRecord
1A:4001.note: wCFEC/wCFED (the first word of the record buffer) = skill number: copies the 17-byte record at SkillTable + 17 * number (bank $1A, $40D4) to wCFEE

1A:4022.name: LoadSkillRecordPart
1A:4022.note: like LoadSkillRecord, but copies wD869 bytes starting wD868 bytes into the record to the address in wD86A/wD86B; with wCFEC = $FF it zero-fills that destination instead

34:4001.name: LoadMonsterRecord
34:4001.note: wCFE6/wCFE7 = monster id: copies its 26-byte MonsterTable record to wCFEC (ids at or above $250 come from bank $A2 through Func_0A2_402D)

34:4040.name: LoadMonsterRecordTo
34:4040.note: DE = destination: like LoadMonsterRecord but copies the 26-byte record to [DE]

34:406E.name: CopyBytesDEFromHL
34:406E.note: B bytes from [HL] to [DE]; HL and DE advance

01:4F80.name: DebugShowMonsterRecord
01:4F80.note: HL = monster id (the debug monster viewer wraps it at $02AB): stores it in wC5F8/wC5F9 and wMonsterId/wCFE7, loads the record with LoadMonsterRecord and draws the id, the name (string bank $88, category = id high byte, index = id low byte) and the record's fields on the debug screen

95:468D.name: StringTable95_Cat09_SkillDescriptions
95:468D.note: string table of category $09 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): skill descriptions, for example 'Attacks an enemy with a fireball' (E-0033)

95:47ED.name: StringTable95_Cat0A
95:47ED.note: string table of category $0A (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): two-line names such as 'VIT Belt', 'Draco Belt', 'Stone Fang' (the table at $47EF is the same list one entry later) (E-0033)

95:47EF.name: StringTable95_Cat0B
95:47EF.note: string table of category $0B (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): the same names as category $0A without the blank first entry (E-0033)

95:4837.name: StringTable95_Cat0C_FieldActions
95:4837.note: string table of category $0C (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): short two-line phrases such as 'Call ship', 'Call cloud', 'Smash rock', 'Burn', 'Cut', 'Open door' (E-0033)

95:4839.name: StringTable95_Cat0D
95:4839.note: string table of category $0D (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): the same phrases as category $0C without the blank first entry (E-0033)

95:4847.name: StringTable95_Cat0E_Tactics
95:4847.note: string table of category $0E (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'Attack', 'Charge', 'Mixed', 'Cautious', 'Command' (E-0033)

95:4853.name: StringTable95_Cat0F
95:4853.note: string table of category $0F (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'Charge', 'Mixed', 'Cautious', 'ZoneOut' (overlaps category $0E) (E-0033)

95:4857.name: StringTable95_Cat10
95:4857.note: string table of category $10 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'Charge', 'Mixed', 'Cautious', 'ZoneOut', 'Chance', 'Confusion', shown for the high nibble of a skill record's byte 3 (E-0033)

95:4869.name: StringTable95_Cat11_Targets
95:4869.note: string table of category $11 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'No area', '1 enemy', 'All enemies', 'Foes multi-hit', '1 friend', 'All friends', 'Choose 1' (E-0033)

95:487F.name: StringTable95_Cat12_SkillFamilies
95:487F.note: string table of category $12 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'None', 'Blaze', 'Firebal', 'Bang', 'Infernos', 'Bolt', 'IceBolt' (E-0033)

95:48B7.name: StringTable95_Cat13_SkillTypes
95:48B7.note: string table of category $13 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'Type A' ... 'Type G' (E-0033)

95:48C7.note: string table of category $14 (the string database extension in bank $95, selected when wStringCategory is 9 or more): 'None', 'Battle', 'Field', 'Anytime' (E-0033)

16:4007.name: LoadItemRecord
16:4007.note: wItemId (wD081) = item id: copies the 13-byte ItemTable record to wItemRecord (wD084)

16:4025.name: CheckItemUsable
16:4025.note: returns when wItemId is $FF; otherwise jumps through a table with one usability check per item id (a check refuses by setting wItemId = $FF; ApplyItemEffect then performs the use, E-0089) (most entries are the shared Jump_016_462F; for example Func_016_40F6 refuses use when the words at save-record offsets $5B and $5D, the monster's current and maximum HP, are equal)

11:4002.name: CheckWarpAtPlayer
11:4002.note: unless a special mode is set (wCC44 bit 7 hands over to Func_061_5764): walks the warp list MapWarpTable[hMapId]; an entry matching hPlayerFacing, the player's position and its screen nibbles starts a map change: wCCEA = 1, sound effect $60 is queued, and the entry's new hMapId, hFF8F, hFF92 and position (wC8C8/wC8C9) are stored

00:19A9.name: LoadMapScreen
00:19A9.note: loads the screen at (hMapScreenX, hMapScreenY) of map hMapId: finds the map record (MapRecordPointer), picks one of its variants by the highest set bit of the flag byte whose RAM address is stored in the record, decompresses that variant's tile-map stream (an array of far pointers, indexed by row * width + column) into wScreenTileBuffer and, on CGB, the attribute stream into wD000 (WRAM bank 2); then runs the map's tile-replacement table (Func_084_43B8) and two map-specific fix-ups (Func_000_1B6F, Func_000_1A73); hands over to Func_061_4472 when wCC44 bit 7 is set

00:1D7F.name: MapRecordPointer
00:1D7F.note: HL = the word at MapTable + 2 * hMapId (bank $11)

00:1BAD.name: LoadSpecialMapHeader
00:1BAD.note: hFFC6 = index into a table at bank $61 $60D8 of special map records: decompresses the first far-pointer stream to vTiles2, handles the second with Func_000_24E5, then stores the next five bytes in wMapWidthScreens, wMapHeightScreens, wMaxBlockingTile, wC193 and wC90D and clears wC901, wC194-wC196

10:4001.name: RunEventScriptFrame
10:4001.note: one frame of the event-script engine: FetchScriptCommand, then ExecuteScriptCommand

10:4008.name: FetchScriptCommand
10:4008.note: does nothing during a fade or unless wScriptStartRequest bit 7 is set (then it clears that bit and sets wScriptRunning); reads the opcode at wScriptPointer (through ReadWordFromDataBank when wScriptInDataBank is set) and jumps through a 13-entry opcode table; $FF ends the script (wScriptRunning, wScriptCommandType and wScriptInDataBank cleared, wModeState = 0, or 5 when wCC44 bit 7 is set); the opcode handlers set wScriptCommandType and its parameters and advance wScriptPointer

10:46E9.name: ExecuteScriptCommand
10:46E9.note: does nothing during a fade or while wScriptCommandType is 0; otherwise jumps through ScriptCommandHandlers[wScriptCommandType - 1] to run one frame of the current command

10:46CD.name: StartEventScript
10:46CD.note: HL = script address: clears wC921-wC926 (parameters and step) and stores HL in wScriptPointer; the script is run by RunEventScriptFrame (28 call sites)

5F:785C.name: ScriptWaitFrames
5F:785C.note: script command 04: wScriptParam0/1 is a 16-bit counter that falls by one each frame; at zero it clears wScriptCommandType and sets wScriptStartRequest = $80 so the next script byte is fetched (the opening's waits of 30, 60 and 90 frames showed the counter at 29, 59 and 89)

5F:77D8.name: ScriptStepObject
5F:77D8.note: script commands 02 and 03 (and 05 through Func_05F_787C): wScriptParam0 low nibble is an object number (16-byte entries from wCB7F), its high nibble a direction 0-3; sets bit 2 of the object's flag byte and moves the object's position by one unit in that direction

10:4486.name: ScriptFetchGeneric
10:4486.note: fetch handler shared by 123 opcodes: wScriptCommandType = the opcode byte, then StartEventScript with the pointer just after it; the command reads its own arguments from the script

10:4248.name: ScriptFetchGeneric2
10:4248.note: the same five instructions as ScriptFetchGeneric, used by 30 opcodes

3B:4001.name: GetBaseHP
3B:4001.note: C = battle slot: returns in wBattleStatResultLo/Hi the slot's base HP: for slot numbers whose low two bits are 3 (slots 3 and 7) the monster id from wDAAE is loaded with LoadMonsterRecord and the monster record's HP word (wCFF6) is returned; otherwise the word at offset $1D of the slot's 78-byte battler record (wBattlerRecords, BattlerRecordFieldAddress).
